title: AI Media Scout — Collage, sound, puppetry and editable production workflows
summary: Today’s expanded review adds practical guides across AI collage, neural sound design, 2D puppetry, avatar motion, video editing, spatial reconstruction, mapping and fabrication. Earlier screened tools receive detailed installation and first-use guidance; additional eligible discoveries enter the library with full-profile work still pending. All platforms receive equal consideration, with documented support and unknown requirements labeled explicitly. Quality remains evidence-based: no tool was installed or run, and no stars or completed guide automatically grant a recommendation. OpenSuno’s current source notices fail the open-source criterion for its integrated workflow; its historical entry remains preserved with a current license warning. The library gains 49 distinct tools; 19 earlier screened entries become full guides. The complete retained catalog was scanned at the metadata level, followed by bounded manual metadata review and targeted primary-source reads beyond the automatic README shortlist, including a final pass after collection. This was not a manual eligibility review of every search result; raw unreviewed matches remain private. All 464 planned repository queries and 18 model tasks were attempted across 61 fields. Repository search outcomes: 464 successful, 0 partial and 0 failed; 109 reached result bounds. Model query failures: 0. Coverage is not exhaustive. All eight configured web ecosystems have researched findings. Some primary pages returned script shells or failed to load; these limitations are disclosed in the field and source-group notes. Model metadata is a discovery signal, not permission to publish unreviewed software. The collection records 118 warnings, including source retrieval and bounded-search disclosures retained in the report coverage details.

Neutone’s model examples and the YOLO-sonification source support adjacent sound practices. The latter still lacks enough documented setup detail for a complete guide; sample-brain’s available path is rule-based with a missing optional embedding module.
Timeflux and Mind Draw Play describe acquisition and audiovisual feedback. The new motion-capture guide separates MediaPipe targets, IMU measurements and missing/timing-error behavior.
Material Apprentice describes generating procedural materials from expert demonstrations. Procedura assigns editable materials to generated assemblies; no new production validation was inferred.

E2VID learns intensity reconstruction from event streams; LenslessPiCam documents sensor/mask and reconstruction requirements. These are specialized acquisition workflows, not ordinary camera-app compatibility.
COrigami’s abstract describes AI crease generation under foldability constraints. A paper and examples alone do not clear implementation licensing or demonstrate a physically successful fold.
GardenDesigner describes agent-guided Jiangnan garden scenes for virtual media. The reviewed demonstration does not certify real landscape engineering or construction suitability.

Neural Collages uses self-similarity for image representation. Today’s collage tools address editable compositions, but traditional mosaics or fractal algorithms without a demonstrated AI stage stay outside scope.
Visual Anagrams and Factorized Diffusion show transformation- and viewing-dependent images. Their primary demos remain useful context; no unchanged tool was recycled as a new profile.

Inverse-halftoning research describes learned image reconstruction. Completed CoinForge Studio with AI background removal and agent design; physical engraving settings and source artwork rights remain separate.
Read compositional and stylized neural-painting research. A brushstroke result or research origin does not establish code eligibility; earlier license gaps are not silently cleared.
Neural Preset describes learned per-pixel color mapping. OBS light matching and ordinary palette arithmetic are conventional components even when connected to an AI workflow.

Read Neural Collage Transfer research and reviewed AI collage editors and composition skills. CollageRL has non-commercial software terms; CollageNet and collage-diffusion-ui lack retrieved licenses. Those research results do not establish eligibility. New eligible composition guides disclose source-art and model terms.

ecosystem_checks.finding: Read the bounded diffusion and music API searches. AudioSR and LongCat mirrors led to completed upstream guides. Many music matches are conventional players, mirrors or deleted projects; no license inference was made from those search descriptions.

The first fifty diffusion results were available through the API. Followed Black Latents into its README and license: the app is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so it remains excluded despite concrete neural-audio relevance. Public page access failed in the web tool; the primary API supplied the evidence.

Read the neural-project listing. Results were mainly generic neural-network tutorials and security research; no additional clearly creative, license-reviewed tool was established. This was a bounded listing, not an exhaustive ecosystem crawl.

Read current Neutone SDK and AudioSR PyPI JSON. The fastgs package is a different geospatial project, not FastGS Gaussian reconstruction; package names are not identity evidence. F-Droid supplied current SDAI platform distinctions.

Reviewed current QGIS listings, AITracer, OBS neural matting, ComfyUI audio nodes and the Neural Morphing VST3 bridge. Complete host, model and runtime requirements remain separate from each plugin grant.

Refreshed primary sites across all sixty-one fields and followed new Iki, OpenChatCut, modl, localpress and Renku sites. Some pages supplied only script shells; three initial URLs failed, including SyncLight TLS. Those failures are not working-demo evidence.

Read collage, scene, neural-audio, capture and physical-media research. Reviewed complete source grants and relevant notices; OpenSuno’s bundled non-commercial code reopens its existing library license check, while FastGS’s earlier hold remains justified.

Read Chinese/English VRMA and image-tool documentation, Vietnamese speech tooling, Portuguese production tooling and the German INTEX case. Language, popularity and research origin are not quality labels.
